title: Speech-to-Speech Model Research at Google DeepMind — Valeria Wu Fon & Tom Ouyang, Google DeepMind
talk_summary: A product/research overview of Google DeepMind's native multimodal speech-to-speech Gemini models, covering live translation, conversational voice agents, and avatar demos. It is almost entirely about audio model capabilities and product vision, with no engineering process, orchestration, or cost techniques.

takeaways.technique: Single promptable model instead of task-specific pipelines
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue one natively multimodal model can be steered by prompting to do translation, agentic tool use, or embodied responses, replacing hand-built cascaded pipelines.
takeaways.evidence_quote: with the LLM and Gemini models, this almost becomes a prompting task

takeaways.technique: Tunable thinking budget vs latency tradeoff
takeaways.what_they_do: They note raising 'thinking' improves eval intelligence but hurts time-to-first-audio and naturalness, so they treat it as a knob to balance per use case.
